clue.text: Seek assistance from leader of the navy, breaking out guns outside

indicators.note: something broken falls apart, so the little word before it is rearranged
a leader comes at the front, so only the opening letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word

indicators.note: outside says the rearranged letters sit around the abbreviation for the navy

parts.note: the word rearranged
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A naval commander asks for help as rebels break out with their guns all around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking out' reads as an escape, but 'breaking' works only on the word 'out'. 'guns' gives G, the first letter of GEOGRAPHICALLY in the down clues.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn to someone is the idiom for going to them for help or support.

clue.text: Openings for Manchester United — Albion to endure shakily in a dangerous position here

parts.note: the first letters of the two words
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A football report: Manchester United's early chances leave a nervous Albion side exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: Albion is a common club name (West Brom, Brighton) and also an old name for Britain, but here it is just letters. 'endure' gives E.
explanation.definitionFit: Being out on a limb is the idiom for being exposed and vulnerable, like someone on a thin branch.

clue.text: Papers from Orwell novel — novel in series

explanation.walkthrough: The two 'novel's do different jobs: the first is the adjective, the second Haggard's book She, which sits inside SETS. 'Orwell' gives O.
explanation.definitionFit: News-sheets are simple newspapers, printed sheets carrying news.

clue.text: Cry about ultimately glib, heartless stud

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for a cry is read backwards

parts.note: to sob is to cry

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so only the last letter is taken

parts.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone complains about a smooth-talking, callous ladies' man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stud' looks like a womaniser, but it is the raised knob sense. 'glib' gives G.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a round raised ornament or knob, the same thing as a decorative stud.

clue.text: Old revolutionary readying place from where missiles are launched

definitions.text: place from where missiles are launched

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
Che Guevara, the Argentine revolutionary

explanation.surface: A veteran rebel prepares a rocket launch site.
explanation.walkthrough: The missiles are darts: the oche is the line a darts player stands behind to throw. 'readying' gives R.
explanation.definitionFit: In darts the oche is the mark behind which players stand to throw, so their missiles are launched from there.

clue.text: Flower from heart of Holland telly in Amsterdam broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast also means scattered widely, as seed is, so the letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: the middle letter of the seven-letter word
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tulip-like bloom shown on Dutch television from Amsterdam.
explanation.walkthrough: Telly is British slang for television. 'Amsterdam' gives A.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lent lily is a country name for the wild daffodil, which blooms around Lent.

clue.text: Croissant? In Paris read article about organic one

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the French words for read and the article wrap round the French for one

explanation.definitionFit: A lunule is a crescent-shaped mark, like the pale half-moon at a fingernail's base; croissant means crescent.

clue.text: Cantankerous recitalist ignoring variable note

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out, so the letter for a variable is dropped

parts.note: crotchety means irritable and cantankerous

explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a crotchet is what Americans call a quarter note. 'recitalist' gives R.
explanation.definitionFit: A crotchet is a musical note of one beat, the quarter note in American terms.

clue.text: Metal prettifying Switzerland's capital

parts.note: CH is the international code for Switzerland
Rome, the Italian capital, is one capital

explanation.surface: Shiny metal being used to smarten up Bern, the Swiss capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switzerland's capital' looks like Bern, or the letter S; the two words are separate pieces. 'prettifying' gives P.
explanation.definitionFit: Chromium, commonly called chrome, is a hard bright metallic element used for plating.

clue.text: Charged matter some Pakistani dumped on ship

indicators.note: only some of the word Pakistani is kept, its closing letters

parts.note: taken as written before its front is shed

explanation.surface: Some Pakistani goods are unloaded onto a vessel and billed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dumped' is the puzzle's extra word, its first letter D going to the message; drop it and the answer runs on from the tail of 'Pakistani' through 'on' and the S of 'ship'.
explanation.definitionFit: These are negatively charged ions, particles of matter carrying an electric charge.

clue.text: Unfinished opera is composed about dry Italian folk enjoying music

definitions.note: the definition is Italian folk music; enjoying is the extra word inside it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Enjoying' is the extra word whose first letter goes to the message. OPER and IS rearranged give RISPEO, around TT.
explanation.definitionFit: A rispetto is a type of Italian folk song in eight-line stanzas, or music in that style.

clue.text: Unjustifiable delay resolving choice between leaders in Malaysia

indicators.note: between puts the word for a choice in the middle of the two initials

explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' looks like a call for first letters, but here they are the initials of two real leaders. 'resolving' gives R.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, especially Scots law, mora is undue delay in asserting a right or claim.

clue.text: American pigment China purchased — money wasted

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 'American' signals the US spelling; in Britain it is haemocyanin. 'purchased' gives P.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemocyanin is the blue copper-based respiratory pigment in the blood of molluscs and crustaceans.

clue.text: Right-wingers prepare special Harrod's hampers

parts.note: Cons is short for Conservatives
to train is to prepare
S is an abbreviation for special

explanation.definitionFit: To constrain is to restrict or hold back, which is what hampering does.

clue.text: Instrument for Cockney, sounding jittery and worried, intent to space notes out

ate, as in 'what's eating you', means worried

explanation.walkthrough: The middle of the answer is said 'edgy' but spelt EGGI. 'intent' gives I.
explanation.definitionFit: To arpeggiate is to play a chord's notes one after another rather than together, spreading them out.

clue.text: Nibble into gold eggs, by the way?

indicators.note: into means going inside, so the word for nibble enters the word for gold

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
to nibble is to take a small bite

explanation.surface: Biting into golden eggs, as an aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eggs' gives E.
explanation.definitionFit: Obiter is Latin for incidentally, familiar from obiter dictum, a remark made in passing.

clue.text: Coming across animal, behave dominantly

parts.note: over means across, as in going over the road
a bear is an animal

explanation.surface: Meeting a wild creature, you should act bold and assertive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming across' reads as a phrase meaning meeting, but only 'across' is wordplay. 'Coming' gives C.
explanation.definitionFit: To overbear is to dominate or overrule others by force of personality, hence overbearing.

clue.text: Atrabilious agent riled about card game

nap, short for Napoleon, is a card game

explanation.walkthrough: Atrabilious literally means full of black bile, the old cause of melancholy and irritability. 'riled' gives R.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone irritable and short-tempered, quick to bite back.

explanation.walkthrough: 'anti-capitalist' gives A.

taken as written

clue.text: In Scotland compelled leaders of mob that's running a government to retreat

clue.text: Drunken seamen holding cask regularly and one ewer with identical handle?

clue.text: Refusal rattling vendor having avoided dismissal
